answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent's reputation to a verifiable chain of work, like a climbing route from a base vertex up to the summit: a new agent starts low and earns trust only through attested contributions that peers can check. A sybil swarm can copy a name, but it cannot copy the accumulated trail of work, so its members stay at the base while real agents rise. Like a comet that leaves a visible trail, every action leaves evidence; cheap identities arrive with no trail at all, and the network can simply ignore voices with nothing behind them.
